memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him all the more. He said to them, 'Listen to this dream I had: We were binding sheaves of grain out in the field when suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around mine and bowed down to it.' His brothers said to him, 'Do you intend to reign over us? Will you actually rule us?' And they hated him all the more because of his dream and what he had said." - Gen 37:5-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph has a dream — sheaves of grain in the field, with his brothers' sheaves bowing down to his. And he tells them about it. Understandably, this does not go over well. "Do you intend to reign over us?" they demand, and their hatred deepens.

Here is a place to hold two truths together. On the one hand, this dream was truly from God. As the story unfolds, it comes to pass exactly — years later, Joseph's brothers really do bow before him in Egypt (Gen 42:6). God was revealing His purposes for Joseph's life ahead of time.

On the other hand, young Joseph seems to have shared the dream without much wisdom, tossing it out to brothers who already resented him. Sometimes what God shows us is meant to be treasured quietly and prayerfully, not broadcast to everyone. Not every God-given insight needs to be announced; some things are better carried in the heart until the right time.

There is a gentle lesson for us in this. When God gives us a sense of His purposes, a dream, or a calling, we can ask for wisdom about when and with whom to share it. Discernment guards us from stirring up needless conflict. Hold God's promises with faith — but also with humility and good timing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust that God reveals His purposes in His own way?
2. Am I wise about when and with whom I share what matters?
3. Where do I need discernment rather than just openness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You reveal Your purposes in Your time. Give me wisdom about what to share and what to treasure quietly, and keep me humble as I trust You with my future. Amen.
